**Texas's 34th congressional district** is a United States congressional district in the southern part of Texas that was created as a result of the [2010 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-4) The first candidates ran in the [2012 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2012 United States House of Representatives elections"); the winner, [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)")[Filemon Vela Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr. "Filemon Vela Jr."), was seated for the [113th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/113th_United_States_Congress "113th United States Congress").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-5) The district is currently represented by [Vicente Gonzalez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Gonzalez_(American_politician) "Vicente Gonzalez (American politician)") ([D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)")-[McAllen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McAllen,_Texas "McAllen, Texas")), who was redistricted there from [Texas's 15th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_15th_congressional_district "Texas's 15th congressional district").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-6)

Texas's 34th congressional district is composed of the area on the Gulf Coast between [Brownsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownsville,_Texas "Brownsville, Texas") and [Corpus Christi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_Christi,_Texas "Corpus Christi, Texas"), the latter of which being situated in the neighboring [27th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_27th_congressional_district "Texas's 27th congressional district").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-7) It extends westward to include the northeastern portion of [McAllen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McAllen,_Texas "McAllen, Texas") and surrounds, with the rest of the [McAllen area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidalgo_County,_Texas "Hidalgo County, Texas") being in the [15th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_15th_congressional_district "Texas's 15th congressional district"). In addition to the City of Brownsville, other major towns in the district include [Alice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice,_Texas "Alice, Texas"), [Beeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beeville,_Texas "Beeville, Texas"), [Harlingen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlingen,_Texas "Harlingen, Texas"), [Kingsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsville,_Texas "Kingsville, Texas") and [San Benito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Benito,_Texas "San Benito, Texas").

The district was one of 13 congressional districts that voted for [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") in the [2024 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election") while simultaneously electing a Democrat in the [2024 House of Representatives elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2024 United States House of Representatives elections").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-8)

**Texas's 34th congressional district** is a United States congressional district in the southern part of Texas that was created as a result of the [2010 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-4) The first candidates ran in the [2012 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2012 United States House of Representatives elections"); the winner, [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)")[Filemon Vela Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr. "Filemon Vela Jr."), was seated for the [113th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/113th_United_States_Congress "113th United States Congress").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-5) The district is currently represented by [Vicente Gonzalez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Gonzalez_(American_politician) "Vicente Gonzalez (American politician)") ([D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)")-[McAllen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McAllen,_Texas "McAllen, Texas")), who was redistricted there from [Texas's 15th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_15th_congressional_district "Texas's 15th congressional district").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-6)

Texas's 34th congressional district is composed of the area on the Gulf Coast between [Brownsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownsville,_Texas "Brownsville, Texas") and [Corpus Christi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_Christi,_Texas "Corpus Christi, Texas"), the latter of which being situated in the neighboring [27th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_27th_congressional_district "Texas's 27th congressional district").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-7) It extends westward to include the northeastern portion of [McAllen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McAllen,_Texas "McAllen, Texas") and surrounds, with the rest of the [McAllen area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidalgo_County,_Texas "Hidalgo County, Texas") being in the [15th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_15th_congressional_district "Texas's 15th congressional district"). In addition to the City of Brownsville, other major towns in the district include [Alice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice,_Texas "Alice, Texas"), [Beeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beeville,_Texas "Beeville, Texas"), [Harlingen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlingen,_Texas "Harlingen, Texas"), [Kingsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingsville,_Texas "Kingsville, Texas") and [San Benito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Benito,_Texas "San Benito, Texas").

The district was one of 13 congressional districts that voted for [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") in the [2024 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election") while simultaneously electing a Democrat in the [2024 House of Representatives elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2024 United States House of Representatives elections").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district#cite_note-8)

**Filemón Bartolomé Vela Jr.** ([/ˈ f ɪ l ə ˌ m ɒ n ˈ v ɛ l ə/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_FILL-ə-monn VELL-ə_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born February 13, 1963)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-1) is an American lobbyist, lawyer, and politician who served as the [U.S. representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") for [Texas's 34th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district "Texas's 34th congressional district") from 2013 until his resignation in 2022. He is a member of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"). Vela was also vice chair of the [Democratic National Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee "Democratic National Committee") from January 21, 2021 to March 31, 2022, having been nominated by President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-2) In March 2022, Vela resigned in the middle of his term to work at [Akin Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akin_Gump_Strauss_Hauer_&_Feld "Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-resign-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-steps_down-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Vela was born in [Harlingen, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlingen,_Texas "Harlingen, Texas"), and raised in nearby [Brownsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownsville,_Texas "Brownsville, Texas"). His father, [Filemon Vela Sr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Sr. "Filemon Vela Sr."), was a long-serving United States federal judge. The Reynaldo G. Garza–Filemon B. Vela United States Courthouse in Brownsville is named in Judge Vela's honor. His mother, [Blanca Sanchez Vela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanca_Vela "Blanca Vela"), served as Brownsville's first female mayor from 1999 to 2003.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-vela.house.gov-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-7)

Filemon attended [Saint Joseph Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph_Academy_(Brownsville,_Texas) "Saint Joseph Academy (Brownsville, Texas)") in Brownsville, and earned his [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") from [Georgetown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University") in 1985. During his time at Georgetown, he served as an intern at the [Federal Judicial Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Judicial_Center "Federal Judicial Center"), the research and education agency of the federal judicial system. He also served as an intern in [Solomon P. Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_P._Ortiz "Solomon P. Ortiz")'s office in Washington, D.C. Vela earned his [Juris Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") from the [University of Texas at Austin School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_School_of_Law "University of Texas School of Law") in 1987.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-vela.house.gov-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

In _[Edinburg School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburg\_Consolidated\_Independent\_School\_District "Edinburg Consolidated Independent School District") v. Landmark_, Vela represented [Edinburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburg,_Texas "Edinburg, Texas") to fight for more funding. In _Pharr-San Juan-Alamo Independent School District v. ## U.S. House of Representatives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: U.S. House of Representatives")]

### Elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Elections")]

#### 2012

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2012")]

Main article: [2012 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas §District 34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Texas#District_34 "2012 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas")

Vela ran in the newly created [34th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district "Texas's 34th congressional district") as a Democrat. In the May 29 primary, he ranked first in an eight-candidate field with 40% of the vote.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-9) In the July 31 runoff, Vela defeated Denise Saenz Blanchard, 67% to 33%.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-11)

In the general election, Vela defeated Republican Jessica Bradshaw, 62% to 36%.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-12)

### Tenure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Tenure")]

In July 2013, Vela quit the [Congressional Hispanic Caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Hispanic_Caucus "Congressional Hispanic Caucus") because of his opposition to the [Hoeven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hoeven "John Hoeven")-[Corker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Corker "Bob Corker") Amendment that tied border security to a [pathway to citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty "Amnesty"). He said "erecting more border fence drives a wedge between border communities which are culturally united".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-14)

On March 22, 2021, Vela announced that he would not seek reelection in the [2022 United States House of Representatives elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2022 United States House of Representatives elections").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-15)

In August 2021, Vela joined a group of conservative Democrats, dubbed "The Unbreakable Nine", who threatened to derail the [Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden#Administration "Presidency of Joe Biden")'s $3.5 trillion budget reconciliation package meant to tackle the nation's infrastructure.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-17)

On March 24, 2022, Vela confirmed that he would resign early from Congress to take a job at [Akin Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akin_Gump "Akin Gump"), a lobbying and law firm.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-resign-3) His resignation officially went into effect before midnight on March 31.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-steps_down-4)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Vela's wife, Rose, was a [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") justice on Texas's 13th [Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Courts_of_Appeals "Texas Courts of Appeals") from 2007 to 2012.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-24)

Vela is [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic "Roman Catholic").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-25)

**Filemón Bartolomé Vela Jr.** ([/ˈ f ɪ l ə ˌ m ɒ n ˈ v ɛ l ə/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_FILL-ə-monn VELL-ə_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born February 13, 1963)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-1) is an American lobbyist, lawyer, and politician who served as the [U.S. representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") for [Texas's 34th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district "Texas's 34th congressional district") from 2013 until his resignation in 2022. He is a member of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"). Vela was also vice chair of the [Democratic National Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee "Democratic National Committee") from January 21, 2021 to March 31, 2022, having been nominated by President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-2) In March 2022, Vela resigned in the middle of his term to work at [Akin Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akin_Gump_Strauss_Hauer_&_Feld "Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-resign-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-steps_down-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Vela was born in [Harlingen, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlingen,_Texas "Harlingen, Texas"), and raised in nearby [Brownsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownsville,_Texas "Brownsville, Texas"). His father, [Filemon Vela Sr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Sr. "Filemon Vela Sr."), was a long-serving United States federal judge. The Reynaldo G. Garza–Filemon B. Vela United States Courthouse in Brownsville is named in Judge Vela's honor. His mother, [Blanca Sanchez Vela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanca_Vela "Blanca Vela"), served as Brownsville's first female mayor from 1999 to 2003.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-vela.house.gov-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-7)

Filemon attended [Saint Joseph Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph_Academy_(Brownsville,_Texas) "Saint Joseph Academy (Brownsville, Texas)") in Brownsville, and earned his [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") from [Georgetown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University") in 1985. During his time at Georgetown, he served as an intern at the [Federal Judicial Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Judicial_Center "Federal Judicial Center"), the research and education agency of the federal judicial system. He also served as an intern in [Solomon P. Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_P._Ortiz "Solomon P. Ortiz")'s office in Washington, D.C. Vela earned his [Juris Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") from the [University of Texas at Austin School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_School_of_Law "University of Texas School of Law") in 1987.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-vela.house.gov-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

In _[Edinburg School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburg\_Consolidated\_Independent\_School\_District "Edinburg Consolidated Independent School District") v. Landmark_, Vela represented [Edinburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburg,_Texas "Edinburg, Texas") to fight for more funding. In _Pharr-San Juan-Alamo Independent School District v. Landmark_, he represented the district in fighting contractors accused of building a poorly constructed school facility.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-8)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

## U.S. House of Representatives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: U.S. House of Representatives")]

### Elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Elections")]

#### 2012

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2012")]

Main article: [2012 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas §District 34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Texas#District_34 "2012 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas")

Vela ran in the newly created [34th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district "Texas's 34th congressional district") as a Democrat. In the May 29 primary, he ranked first in an eight-candidate field with 40% of the vote.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-9) In the July 31 runoff, Vela defeated Denise Saenz Blanchard, 67% to 33%.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-11)

In the general election, Vela defeated Republican Jessica Bradshaw, 62% to 36%.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-12)

### Tenure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Tenure")]

In July 2013, Vela quit the [Congressional Hispanic Caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Hispanic_Caucus "Congressional Hispanic Caucus") because of his opposition to the [Hoeven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hoeven "John Hoeven")-[Corker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Corker "Bob Corker") Amendment that tied border security to a [pathway to citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty "Amnesty"). He said "erecting more border fence drives a wedge between border communities which are culturally united".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-14)

On March 22, 2021, Vela announced that he would not seek reelection in the [2022 United States House of Representatives elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2022 United States House of Representatives elections").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-15)

In August 2021, Vela joined a group of conservative Democrats, dubbed "The Unbreakable Nine", who threatened to derail the [Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden#Administration "Presidency of Joe Biden")'s $3.5 trillion budget reconciliation package meant to tackle the nation's infrastructure.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-17)

On March 24, 2022, Vela confirmed that he would resign early from Congress to take a job at [Akin Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akin_Gump "Akin Gump"), a lobbying and law firm.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-resign-3) His resignation officially went into effect before midnight on March 31.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-steps_down-4)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Vela's wife, Rose, was a [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") justice on Texas's 13th [Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Courts_of_Appeals "Texas Courts of Appeals") from 2007 to 2012.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-24)

Vela is [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic "Roman Catholic").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Jr.#cite_note-25)

**Filemón Bartolomé Vela Jr.** ([/ˈ f ɪ l ə ˌ m ɒ n ˈ v ɛ l ə/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_FILL-ə-monn VELL-ə_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born February 13, 1963)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-1) is an American lobbyist, lawyer, and politician who served as the [U.S. representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") for [Texas's 34th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district "Texas's 34th congressional district") from 2013 until his resignation in 2022. He is a member of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"). Vela was also vice chair of the [Democratic National Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee "Democratic National Committee") from January 21, 2021 to March 31, 2022, having been nominated by President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-2) In March 2022, Vela resigned in the middle of his term to work at [Akin Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akin_Gump_Strauss_Hauer_&_Feld "Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-resign-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-steps_down-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Vela was born in [Harlingen, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlingen,_Texas "Harlingen, Texas"), and raised in nearby [Brownsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownsville,_Texas "Brownsville, Texas"). His father, [Filemon Vela Sr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Sr. "Filemon Vela Sr."), was a long-serving United States federal judge. The Reynaldo G. Garza–Filemon B. Vela United States Courthouse in Brownsville is named in Judge Vela's honor. His mother, [Blanca Sanchez Vela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanca_Vela "Blanca Vela"), served as Brownsville's first female mayor from 1999 to 2003.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-vela.house.gov-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-7)

Filemon attended [Saint Joseph Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph_Academy_(Brownsville,_Texas) "Saint Joseph Academy (Brownsville, Texas)") in Brownsville, and earned his [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") from [Georgetown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University") in 1985. During his time at Georgetown, he served as an intern at the [Federal Judicial Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Judicial_Center "Federal Judicial Center"), the research and education agency of the federal judicial system. He also served as an intern in [Solomon P. Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_P._Ortiz "Solomon P. Ortiz")'s office in Washington, D.C. Vela earned his [Juris Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") from the [University of Texas at Austin School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_School_of_Law "University of Texas School of Law") in 1987.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-vela.house.gov-5)

## U.S. House of Representatives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: U.S. House of Representatives")]

### Elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Elections")]

#### 2012

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2012")]

Main article: [2012 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas §District 34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Texas#District_34 "2012 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas")

Vela ran in the newly created [34th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district "Texas's 34th congressional district") as a Democrat. In the May 29 primary, he ranked first in an eight-candidate field with 40% of the vote.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-9) In the July 31 runoff, Vela defeated Denise Saenz Blanchard, 67% to 33%.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-11)

In the general election, Vela defeated Republican Jessica Bradshaw, 62% to 36%.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-12)

### Tenure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Tenure")]

In July 2013, Vela quit the [Congressional Hispanic Caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Hispanic_Caucus "Congressional Hispanic Caucus") because of his opposition to the [Hoeven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hoeven "John Hoeven")-[Corker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Corker "Bob Corker") Amendment that tied border security to a [pathway to citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty "Amnesty"). He said "erecting more border fence drives a wedge between border communities which are culturally united".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-14)

On March 22, 2021, Vela announced that he would not seek reelection in the [2022 United States House of Representatives elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2022 United States House of Representatives elections").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-15)

In August 2021, Vela joined a group of conservative Democrats, dubbed "The Unbreakable Nine", who threatened to derail the [Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden#Administration "Presidency of Joe Biden")'s $3.5 trillion budget reconciliation package meant to tackle the nation's infrastructure.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-17)

On March 24, 2022, Vela confirmed that he would resign early from Congress to take a job at [Akin Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akin_Gump "Akin Gump"), a lobbying and law firm.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-resign-3) His resignation officially went into effect before midnight on March 31.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-steps_down-4)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Vela's wife, Rose, was a [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") justice on Texas's 13th [Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Courts_of_Appeals "Texas Courts of Appeals") from 2007 to 2012.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-24)

Vela is [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic "Roman Catholic").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-25)

**Filemón Bartolomé Vela Jr.** ([/ˈ f ɪ l ə ˌ m ɒ n ˈ v ɛ l ə/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_FILL-ə-monn VELL-ə_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born February 13, 1963)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-1) is an American lobbyist, lawyer, and politician who served as the [U.S. representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") for [Texas's 34th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district "Texas's 34th congressional district") from 2013 until his resignation in 2022. He is a member of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)"). Vela was also vice chair of the [Democratic National Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee "Democratic National Committee") from January 21, 2021 to March 31, 2022, having been nominated by President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-2) In March 2022, Vela resigned in the middle of his term to work at [Akin Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akin_Gump_Strauss_Hauer_&_Feld "Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-resign-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-steps_down-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Vela was born in [Harlingen, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlingen,_Texas "Harlingen, Texas"), and raised in nearby [Brownsville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownsville,_Texas "Brownsville, Texas"). His father, [Filemon Vela Sr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filemon_Vela_Sr. "Filemon Vela Sr."), was a long-serving United States federal judge. The Reynaldo G. Garza–Filemon B. Vela United States Courthouse in Brownsville is named in Judge Vela's honor. His mother, [Blanca Sanchez Vela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanca_Vela "Blanca Vela"), served as Brownsville's first female mayor from 1999 to 2003.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-vela.house.gov-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-7)

Filemon attended [Saint Joseph Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph_Academy_(Brownsville,_Texas) "Saint Joseph Academy (Brownsville, Texas)") in Brownsville, and earned his [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") from [Georgetown University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_University "Georgetown University") in 1985. During his time at Georgetown, he served as an intern at the [Federal Judicial Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Judicial_Center "Federal Judicial Center"), the research and education agency of the federal judicial system. He also served as an intern in [Solomon P. Ortiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_P._Ortiz "Solomon P. Ortiz")'s office in Washington, D.C. Vela earned his [Juris Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") from the [University of Texas at Austin School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Texas_School_of_Law "University of Texas School of Law") in 1987.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-vela.house.gov-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

In _[Edinburg School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburg\_Consolidated\_Independent\_School\_District "Edinburg Consolidated Independent School District") v. Landmark_, Vela represented [Edinburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburg,_Texas "Edinburg, Texas") to fight for more funding. In _Pharr-San Juan-Alamo Independent School District v. Landmark_, he represented the district in fighting contractors accused of building a poorly constructed school facility.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-8)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

## U.S. House of Representatives

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: U.S. House of Representatives")]

### Elections

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Elections")]

#### 2012

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2012")]

Main article: [2012 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas §District 34](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections_in_Texas#District_34 "2012 United States House of Representatives elections in Texas")

Vela ran in the newly created [34th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas's_34th_congressional_district "Texas's 34th congressional district") as a Democrat. In the May 29 primary, he ranked first in an eight-candidate field with 40% of the vote.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-9) In the July 31 runoff, Vela defeated Denise Saenz Blanchard, 67% to 33%.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-11)

In the general election, Vela defeated Republican Jessica Bradshaw, 62% to 36%.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-12)

### Tenure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Tenure")]

In July 2013, Vela quit the [Congressional Hispanic Caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Hispanic_Caucus "Congressional Hispanic Caucus") because of his opposition to the [Hoeven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hoeven "John Hoeven")-[Corker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Corker "Bob Corker") Amendment that tied border security to a [pathway to citizenship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty "Amnesty"). He said "erecting more border fence drives a wedge between border communities which are culturally united".[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-14)

On March 22, 2021, Vela announced that he would not seek reelection in the [2022 United States House of Representatives elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "2022 United States House of Representatives elections").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-15)

In August 2021, Vela joined a group of conservative Democrats, dubbed "The Unbreakable Nine", who threatened to derail the [Biden administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden#Administration "Presidency of Joe Biden")'s $3.5 trillion budget reconciliation package meant to tackle the nation's infrastructure.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-17)

On March 24, 2022, Vela confirmed that he would resign early from Congress to take a job at [Akin Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akin_Gump "Akin Gump"), a lobbying and law firm.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-resign-3) His resignation officially went into effect before midnight on March 31.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-steps_down-4)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Vela's wife, Rose, was a [Republican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") justice on Texas's 13th [Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Courts_of_Appeals "Texas Courts of Appeals") from 2007 to 2012.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-24)

Vela is [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic "Roman Catholic").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Filemon_Vela_Jr.&search=roll#cite_note-25)

### Missed Votes
